sentences.text: (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY)
Though this appeal is posted for admission today, with the consent of both the parties, the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. The appellant/de-facto complainant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 24.11.2025 of the learned III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur, sitting at Sindhanoor in Spl.C.
No.5076/2024, acquitting the accused No.1 for the offences punishable under Section 341, 363, 376 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act and acquitting accused No.2 to 4 of the offences punishable under Section 341, 363, 323, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 17 of POCSO Act, has filed the present appeal.

entities.text: III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Facts that can be gathered from the judgment of the Trial Court are that a prosecution was launched by the complainant by informing the police on 15.10.2021 NC: 2026:KHC-K:810-DB HC-KAR that his daughter was kidnapped by the accused No.1 and the other accused abetted the offence.

The police registered a case for the offences punishable under Section 341, 363, 504,109,
323, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The accused No.1 and the girl were traced from Maski.
After interrogation, the girl disclosed that she was kidnapped by accused No.1 and accused No.2 to 4 instigated him.
She also disclosed that she was taken to Bengaluru and that on 10.09.2021 and two three times thereafter, accused No.1 had forcible sexual intercourse.
The victim girl was found to be a minor.

The Investigating Officer after drawing relevant Mahazars and subjecting the accused No.1 and the girl to medical examination and securing all medical evidence laid a charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 341, 363, 506, 376 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012 against accused No.1 and under Section 341, 363, 506, 376 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012 against accused NC:
2026:KHC-K:810-DB HC-KAR No.2 and accused No.3 and under Sections 323, 341, 504, 506, 109 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 17 of POCSO Act, 2012 against accused No.4.
The copies of the charge sheet were furnished to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

In support of the case of prosecution, the girl was examined as PW.1, Mahazer witnesses, the complainant as PW.5, the mother of the girl as PW.6, the Doctors who examined the accused No.1 and victim as PW.7 and PW.8 and the Head Master of the School as PW.9 and other witnesses and marked Ex.P.1 to P.30.
No material objects were marked.
The accused in their statement under Section 313 denied the evidence of the prosecution witnesses.
Based on the evidence adduced, the Trial Court held that the prosecution failed to prove the charges and acquitted all the accused.
Being aggrieved by the said Judgment, the complainant has filed this appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/the father of victim and learned Addl.
SPP for the respondent NC: 2026:KHC-K:810-DB HC-KAR No.1/complainant State.
Perused the relevant materials furnished by the learned counsel for the appellant.
5. The only question that arises for our consideration is whether the impugned judgment warrants interference at the instance of the de-facto complainant.

6. In the impugned judgment even though the Trial Court has come to the conclusion that the victim is below the age of 18 years as on the date of alleged offence, it has held that the prosecution has failed to prove the offences alleged, as the victim turned hostile to the case of prosecution.

sentences.text: The evidence of material witnesses regarding kidnap and sexual assault is based on the information said to have been given by the victim.

The medical evidence on record in the form of oral evidence of PW8 and the report at Ex.P13 would show that at the time of examination of the victim, her hymen was intact and there were no signs of NC: 2026:KHC-K:810-DB HC-KAR forceful sexual assault.
Further, on the basis of FSL report at Ex.P13, PW8 has opined that there was no evidence suggestive of sexual assault on the victim.
Hence, this Court is of the considered view that on the materials on record there is no prima facie case to show that the respondents No.1 to 4 have committed the offences charged.

7. Further, it is forthcoming in the impugned judgment that in the statement of the accused No.1 recorded by the Trial Court under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., it is mentioned that accused No.1 married the victim and their marriage has been registered.

As per the certificate of registration of marriage,
the date of marriage of the accused No.1 and victim is 15.08.2024, which would show that during the pendency of the case before the Trial Court the respondent No.2/accused No.1 married the victim.
8. Moreover, it is pertinent to note that the respondent No.1/complainant State has not chosen to NC: 2026:KHC-K:810-DB HC-KAR challenge the impugned judgment of acquittal.
Hence, there is absolutely no material to interfere with the impugned judgment of the Trial Court, wherein the respondents No.2 to 5 are acquitted of the offences charged against them in the case.
9. In the result, this appeal is hereby dismissed.

10. Consequently, the impugned judgment dated 24.11.2025 of the learned III Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Raichur, sitting at Sindhanoor and Special Judge for trial of case under POCSO Act,
in Spl.Case No.5076/2024 shall stand confirmed.
